title: OOP y modelo de dominio

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts marked USABLE count as learned.

live_site.note: GitHub Pages fetch returned DisabledError; no source/render parity claim.

confirmed_findings.evidence: OOP is not expanded at first use; CP-N1-C, matching/familiaridad and puertos testeables appear before a stable learner-facing definition.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner recognizes labels without knowing whether they denote a paradigm, project increment, system, process or interface boundary.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Expand Programación Orientada a Objetos (OOP) and CP-N1-C once; define matching/familiaridad by function and delay port terminology until Protocol.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson says a named type has fixed boxes whose required fields cannot be left empty and prevents one field being text in one function and numeric in another. The first dataclass does not enforce type hints or non-empty values at runtime.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner believes changing dict to dataclass automatically validates runtime types and required semantic values.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Separate named structure, static annotations and runtime validation; state that dataclass/type hints alone do not enforce domain validity.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The first class example starts with @dataclass, generated __init__/__repr__, field and default_factory before showing the basic class-instance-state-method mechanism or self.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can instantiate a dataclass but cannot explain where instance attributes come from or how a normal class initializes state.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Show one tiny ordinary class with __init__, self and one method before introducing @dataclass as generated boilerplate.

confirmed_findings.evidence: jobRelevance defines a valid client as having email and DNI; ClientRecord gives emails an empty default, validates only client_id/document_id, and does not validate full_name.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot tell which ClientRecord fields are actually required and can construct an object that violates the stated domain contract.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Choose and state one client invariant set, then enforce every required field consistently in the canonical class.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Invariants are defined as conditions the object always satisfies, but ClientRecord is mutable. After construction c.document_id = '' leaves a live object violating the validated rule.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner equates constructor validation with preservation of an invariant for the object's whole lifetime.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Either freeze/protect invariant-bearing fields or define the rule honestly as construction-time validation and teach how allowed mutations preserve validity.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Opening says CaseFile cannot sustain a relationship without at least one RelationshipEvidence; composition.py constructs CaseFile(entity=ResolvedEntity('E1')) with evidences=[] as valid.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner sees an explicit invariant violated by the canonical example without any failure.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Remove that claimed invariant or require evidence at construction/use an explicit draft state.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Opening says Transaction amount cannot be negative, which permits zero; T1-B later says amount must be positive and rejects amount <= 0.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Boundary value 0 has two different contracts.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Choose non-negative or strictly positive and use it everywhere, including tests.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The gate promises four explicit types ClientRecord, ResolvedEntity, Transaction and RelationshipEvidence, but theory never provides a canonical Transaction class implementation; Transaction exists only in prose.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner reaches practice without a worked model for one quarter of the required domain types and its monetary invariant.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add a minimal Transaction dataclass with amount/currency validation in theory.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose says @property exposes derived fields without dangerous external mutation and raw email remains in an internal field for authorized boundaries, but emails is a public mutable list and can be appended/replaced directly.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner believes adding a property protects underlying mutable public state or enforces authorization.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: State that property controls only that property access; make sensitive state private/read-only by design or return immutable/copy views and define authorization outside the property.

confirmed_findings.evidence: frozen=True is described as preventing object mutation. Dataclasses emulate read-only field assignment; mutable objects stored inside a frozen dataclass can still mutate.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner treats frozen as deep immutability.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say frozen prevents normal reassignment/deletion of fields, not mutation inside mutable field values; prefer immutable field types for hashable value objects.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Hash is glossed as a fixed number. Python salts str hashes, so a dataclass hash based on entity_id strings can differ across interpreter processes even while remaining valid for local sets/dicts.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner may persist or compare Python hash values as stable entity identifiers across runs.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Clarify that hash must stay stable while an object is used in a hashed collection during a run; it is not a persistent identifier.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose implies @runtime_checkable isinstance verifies the Protocol contract at runtime. Python documents that runtime-checkable protocols check attribute presence only, not method signatures or annotated types. A WrongStore with wrong get/save signatures still passes isinstance.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner treats isinstance(store, EntityStore) as runtime interface validation.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach Protocol primarily as a static structural contract; label runtime_checkable as a shallow presence check.

confirmed_findings.evidence: After teaching named domain types, EntityStore.get/save revert to Optional[dict]/dict and FakeStore stores anonymous dictionaries.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The port erases the domain types exactly at the architecture boundary where the lesson claims named types matter.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Define the port in terms of a domain type such as ResolvedEntity or ClientRecord; use DTO dicts only at an explicitly named serialization adapter.

confirmed_findings.evidence: ClientService is typed directly to InMemoryClientRepository rather than EntityStore, and the repository get/save signatures use ClientRecord while the earlier EntityStore Protocol uses dict. The taught port is not used by the service it was supposed to decouple.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot see structural substitution or swap FakeStore/real adapter without changing the service contract.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use one Protocol whose methods operate on the same domain type, then annotate ClientService(repo: ClientRepository).

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose says to_dict/from_dict live at the serialization boundary and are not mixed into business entities; code defines ClientRecord.to_dict on the entity itself and provides no from_dict boundary object/function.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner receives two incompatible meanings of where serialization belongs.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Either explicitly choose entity serialization methods and defend that tradeoff, or move mapping to named adapter functions/classes outside the entity.

confirmed_findings.evidence: ClientRecord is redefined without validate/__post_init__. ClientService.register('', '', '', '') constructs and stores an invalid object despite T1-B's invariant contract.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner learns that later examples may silently discard earlier invariants while retaining the same class name.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Reuse one canonical domain model across subtopics instead of redefining weakened versions.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Prose says tests verify finiteness, range, canonical pair and no verdicts. The test redefines RelationshipEvidence without __post_init__ and tests only one valid score plus two hasattr checks. Non-finite, out-of-range and reversed pairs still construct successfully in that class.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner sees PASS while none of the central validity rules are executable in the class under test.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Import/reuse the canonical RelationshipEvidence and add negative tests for reversed/equal ids, NaN/inf and scores outside [0,1].

confirmed_findings.evidence: Absence checks for two exact method names are presented as protection of the ethical product boundary.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can add an equivalent automatic verdict under another method name and still pass the supposed ethics gate.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Describe these asserts as narrow API regression checks; protect the broader boundary through documented prohibited capabilities plus review/tests of public outputs.

confirmed_findings.evidence: In the first canonical OOP lesson, the core composition/Protocol sequence also introduces subtype, mixin, MRO, ABC, YAGNI, duck typing, static checking, runtime_checkable and adapters.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner must distinguish multiple abstraction mechanisms before the basic class/object/composition model is stable.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Keep core to class-instance, composition and one Protocol port; move mixin/MRO/ABC comparison to optional extension.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Synthetic email/name examples are called 'PII sintética (información personal identificable de mentira)' and the prose invokes 'export legal/backoffice autorizado' without defining any real authorization model.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can confuse synthetic lookalike data with actual PII classification and mistake a prose label for access control.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say 'datos sintéticos con forma de datos personales, que no corresponden a personas reales'; treat authorization as an external system responsibility.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Type hints are described as telling the verifier which values a field admits, but prior type-hint mastery was not creditable and the local text does not restate that Python does not enforce these annotations at runtime.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can read ': str' as runtime admission control.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one sentence: annotations help readers/type checkers; runtime validity still requires explicit validation when the domain needs it.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The first Protocol example simultaneously adds from __future__ import annotations, legacy Dict/Optional forms, Protocol, runtime_checkable and runtime isinstance despite the course targeting Python 3.12+.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The structural-typing idea is buried beneath unrelated annotation compatibility syntax.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use Python 3.12 forms (dict[str, T], T | None), omit future annotations unless needed, and demonstrate static Protocol conformance before runtime_checkable.

execution_checks.observed: After successful construction, assigning document_id='' succeeds and leaves invalid state.
ClientRecord-like dataclass accepted full_name=123 and emails='not-a-list'.
A class with get/save attributes but incompatible signatures passed isinstance(..., runtime_checkable Protocol).
A frozen dataclass containing a list allowed list.append; hash failed with TypeError.
Two interpreter processes produced different hashes for the same frozen dataclass whose compared field was a string.
The simplified repo/service ClientRecord accepted and stored empty ids/name/email.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: field(compare=False) fails to remove display_name from generated equality/hash
rejected_hypotheses.reason: For the frozen dataclass shown, dataclasses uses compare for generated equality and default hash participation; the example's equality-by-entity_id works.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: left_id < right_id fails to reject identical endpoints
rejected_hypotheses.reason: For equal ids, left_id < right_id is false and the canonical RelationshipEvidence raises ValueError.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: canonical pair alone promises complete deduplication of every repeated evidence record
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The text specifically discusses reverse-order pair canonicalization; it does not explicitly promise duplicate-record suppression.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: using Decimal for all scores is required
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The Decimal contract in earlier sections is for money; a bounded finite similarity score may legitimately be float.

rejected_hypotheses.hypothesis: a repository pattern is inherently too advanced for S11
rejected_hypotheses.reason: The roadmap explicitly places repositories/services and domain boundaries in S11; the defect is inconsistent integration, not the topic's existence.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Hasta aquí un cliente ha sido un diccionario... el mismo campo sea texto... y número...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Hasta aquí representamos clientes con diccionarios flexibles. Una clase con campos nombrados reduce errores de nombres y hace visible la estructura esperada, pero no valida automáticamente los tipos ni las reglas del negocio: esas garantías requieren anotaciones para el análisis estático y validación explícita en runtime.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: un tipo con nombre es un formulario impreso... casillas obligatorias no se pueden dejar vacías
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un tipo con nombre funciona como un formulario con casillas conocidas. El formulario describe qué campos existen; las reglas que dicen cuáles son obligatorios o qué valores son válidos deben escribirse y probarse explícitamente.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Los invariantes... tienen que ser ciertas siempre... Transaction no puede... CaseFile no puede...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un invariante es una condición que el diseño decide preservar durante todos los estados válidos de un objeto. Validarla al construir es solo el primer paso: si el objeto puede mutar, cada mutación permitida también debe conservarla. Define de forma única los límites, por ejemplo si amount debe ser > 0 o >= 0, y no declares invariantes que la clase permita violar.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: RelationshipEvidence guarda señales... ninguna clase emite un veredicto
paragraph_audit.improved_content: RelationshipEvidence guarda señales y puntajes de evidencia; ninguna clase de esta sección debe convertirlos automáticamente en una declaración de fraude o parentesco. Un score es una medición para revisión, no una conclusión legal sobre una persona.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: ¿qué tiene que ser verdad para que este objeto pueda existir?... dataclass, propiedades, composición y Protocol
paragraph_audit.improved_content: La pregunta base es: ¿qué estado representa este objeto y qué reglas deben conservarse para que siga siendo válido? Empezaremos con clase, instancia, atributos y métodos; después usaremos dataclass para reducir boilerplate, composición para agrupar objetos y finalmente un Protocol pequeño para desacoplar almacenamiento.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Bloque de referencia...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Bloque de referencia: orden de subtemas, alcance y criterio de cierre.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: T1 introduce objetos y dataclass...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: T1 construye primero el modelo clase→instancia→estado→método y después introduce dataclass e invariantes. T2 trata encapsulación e identidad. T3 composición y un puerto Protocol. T4 integra repositorio/servicio y pruebas del dominio.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Datos sintéticos peruanos...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Caso de laboratorio con datos sintéticos que no pertenecen a personas reales: ids C00x/E0x, correos @ejemplo.pe y montos Decimal en PEN/USD.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Los cuatro tipos con sus invariantes...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: El cierre exige implementaciones visibles y consistentes de ClientRecord, ResolvedEntity, Transaction y RelationshipEvidence, cada una con las reglas que realmente hace cumplir, además de pruebas puras y límites éticos documentados.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Nunca datos personales reales...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Usa únicamente datos sintéticos y no expongas una API que convierta automáticamente scores en veredictos de fraude o parentesco.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Una clase define el molde... @dataclass genera __init__ y __repr__
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Una clase define un nuevo tipo; una instancia es un objeto concreto de ese tipo. Antes de dataclass, muestra cómo __init__ recibe argumentos y los asigna a atributos mediante self. Después explica que @dataclass genera ese boilerplate para campos declarados.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: type hints... qué valores admite... default_factory...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Las anotaciones como client_id: str comunican el tipo esperado a lectores y herramientas de análisis; Python no las usa por sí solo para rechazar un valor incorrecto en runtime. default_factory=list crea una lista nueva por instancia y evita compartir un mismo default mutable.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Migrar dicts... habilita invariantes... PII sintética de mentira
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Migrar de dicts a tipos con nombre hace visible la estructura; las invariantes aparecen solo cuando las implementas. Los ejemplos usan datos sintéticos con forma de datos personales, pero no corresponden a personas reales.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: __post_init__ valida al instante... objeto a medias...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: __post_init__ permite rechazar un estado inicial inválido antes de devolver la instancia al caller. Eso protege la construcción, no todas las mutaciones futuras; si una regla debe ser invariante, las operaciones posteriores también deben preservarla.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: validate reutilizable... factories... rehidratación desde JSON
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Centraliza reglas de dominio en un único lugar. Un factory o adaptador de deserialización convierte el dato externo y llama al constructor canónico, de modo que la misma validación se aplique a toda ruta de entrada.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: sin side-effects de negocio... no llames APIs...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Mantén la validación del estado libre de I/O: no llames red ni disco ni corrijas silenciosamente valores de negocio dentro del constructor.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Transaction amount positivo... PEN/USD...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Define Transaction explícitamente y fija una sola regla de amount. Por ejemplo, si el curso decide que una transacción de este modelo debe ser estrictamente positiva, valida amount > 0 y currency in {'PEN','USD'} en __post_init__, y prueba 0, negativos y moneda no permitida.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: @property... sin mutación peligrosa desde afuera... raw queda interno
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Una property controla cómo se calcula o expone ese atributo, pero no vuelve privados los demás campos. Si el email raw requiere acceso restringido, el diseño debe limitar su exposición explícitamente; una lista pública emails sigue siendo mutable desde afuera.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Métodos de instancia encapsulan consultas puras... sentinel...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Usa properties/métodos de consulta para cálculos locales sin I/O. Cuando falta email, devuelve un resultado documentado o modela la ausencia explícitamente; no dependas de IndexError para representar un caso de dominio.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: setters validados... frozen... nueva instancia
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Si la mutación no forma parte del dominio, prefiere una nueva instancia o frozen. Recuerda que frozen bloquea la reasignación normal de campos, pero no vuelve inmutables los objetos mutables guardados dentro de ellos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: ResolvedEntity usa entity_id estable, no document_id
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Define la identidad de ResolvedEntity mediante un entity_id interno y estable del sistema, no mediante un documento personal que puede corregirse o reemitirse.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: frozen=True... habilita hash seguro... número fijo
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Con eq=True y frozen=True, dataclass puede generar __hash__ cuando los campos comparados son hashables. Ese hash sirve para sets/dicts durante la ejecución; no es un identificador persistente y puede cambiar entre procesos. Frozen tampoco produce inmutabilidad profunda de listas/dicts contenidos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: field(compare=False)... display_name... dataclasses.replace
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Usa compare=False solo cuando el campo no participa en la identidad lógica. En el ejemplo, corregir display_name crea otra instancia que sigue siendo igual por entity_id; documenta esa decisión porque cambia la semántica de ==.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Value objects frozen; agregados CaseFile mutables
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un value object suele ser inmutable por diseño; un agregado puede mutar mediante métodos que preserven sus invariantes. No expongas mutaciones directas que permitan estados inválidos fuera de esos métodos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: has-a también llamada composición...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Composición significa que un objeto contiene o colabora con otros objetos; úsala cuando la relación sea tiene-un y no es-un.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: No fuerces Client(PersonInfo(BaseEntity))...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: No construyas una jerarquía de herencia solo para reutilizar uno o dos campos; extrae comportamiento o compón objetos cuando esa relación describa mejor el dominio.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: par canónico... score finito [0,1]...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un par canónico ordena los ids de una relación no dirigida para representar (E1,E2) y (E2,E1) de la misma forma. Esto normaliza orientación; no sustituye una política separada de deduplicación de registros repetidos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: herencia solo subtipo real... mixins... MRO...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Introduce herencia solo como contraste: úsala cuando una subclase realmente pueda sustituir a su clase base. Deja mixins, MRO y ABC como extensión opcional después de dominar composición.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: composición mantiene dominio auditable... score no veredicto
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Mantén explícito en el README que signal_score es evidencia de matching para revisión y no un veredicto de fraude o parentesco.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Protocol... cualquier objeto con esos métodos cumple... runtime_checkable isinstance
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Protocol describe estructuralmente qué métodos y firmas espera un puerto para herramientas de type checking. @runtime_checkable permite isinstance, pero esa comprobación runtime es superficial: verifica presencia de atributos, no que sus firmas/tipos sean correctos.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: fakes... no acoplar... adaptador real...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Define el puerto con el mismo tipo de dominio que usará el service, por ejemplo ClientRepository.get(...) -> ClientRecord | None y save(ClientRecord). El fake y el adaptador real implementan esa misma forma; dicts pertenecen al borde de serialización.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: No introduzcas Protocol por si acaso... YAGNI...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Usa Protocol cuando realmente necesitas intercambiar al menos dos implementaciones —por ejemplo fake y adaptador real— y muestra esa sustitución en el mismo ejemplo.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Repository light... Service... to_dict/from_dict viven en borde
paragraph_audit.improved_content: El repository oculta almacenamiento detrás de un puerto tipado; el service coordina reglas de dominio sin CLI/HTTP. Elige una frontera de serialización explícita: si los mappers viven fuera de la entidad, implementa to_dict/from_dict como adaptadores y no como métodos del objeto.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: DTOs... notas backoffice... no contraseñas
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Un DTO puede contener solo los campos necesarios para cruzar una frontera. No confundas una exclusión de campos con control de acceso: autorización, almacenamiento y logging siguen siendo responsabilidades separadas.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: CLI S10 llama service... register(...) -> dict
paragraph_audit.improved_content: ClientService debe recibir el Protocol del repositorio y construir el mismo ClientRecord canónico con invariantes. Después un mapper de borde convierte la entidad al formato requerido por CLI u otra salida.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Tests del dominio puros... fakes...
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Prueba el dominio sin red ni base real; un fake del mismo Protocol permite ejercitar reglas y servicios de forma rápida y determinista.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: Assert de invariantes y ausencia de APIs peligrosas... protege límite legal
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Los tests de invariantes deben incluir casos inválidos que demuestren que la clase rechaza estados prohibidos. Los asserts de ausencia de nombres como is_fraud son solo regresiones de API; el límite ético completo también requiere revisar outputs y capacidades públicas.

paragraph_audit.current_excerpt: test verifica finitud, rango, par canónico y no veredictos
paragraph_audit.improved_content: Ejecuta esos cuatro contratos sobre la misma RelationshipEvidence canónica: casos NaN/inf, score <0/>1, ids iguales/revertidos y ausencia de APIs de veredicto. No redefinas una clase más débil solo para el test.

S12_watchlist: S12 must not assume invariant mastery; S11 still conflates construction validation with lifecycle preservation.
S12 adapters/repos must not assume Protocol runtime isinstance validates method signatures.
S12 must reuse one canonical domain model; S11 redefined ClientRecord/RelationshipEvidence with incompatible invariants across examples.
S12 database/API serialization must explicitly choose DTO/mapping boundaries because S11 prose and code contradict each other about to_dict/from_dict placement.
S12 must not assume properties or frozen provide deep encapsulation or authorization.
Transaction monetary contract is not creditable until zero/non-negative policy and canonical implementation are repaired.
CP-N1-C/CASO internal labels remain widow terms unless globally expanded.

summary.most_common_original_problem: The prose states stronger object guarantees than the demonstrated classes actually enforce.
summary.most_important_global_improvement: Use one canonical domain model across all subtopics and distinguish structure, static typing, construction validation and lifecycle invariants.
